To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

wireless data acquisition of time-domain data is possible for miniaturized, battery-operated, mobile, field-portables spectrometers, but the wireless communication protocols that are currently available are not ideal, and new wireless communication protocols are required.

wireless data acquisition using ZigBee, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and UWB is well suited to data acquisition of optical signals from miniaturized, battery-powered, field-portable optical instruments, including spectrometers and detectors, for use in mobile spectrometry.
wireless data acquisition using smartphones and handhelds offers increased flexibility, it has low cost, and it is suitable for mobile spectrometric applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
miniaturizing the laboratory for chemical analysis in a field environment and with wireless data acquisition for chemical analysis on the go.
miniaturizing, field-portable, and wireless spectrometers, detectors, and optical emission sources.
development and application of wireless data acquisition using smartphones and handhelds for mobile spectrometric applications.

the wireless communications standards that are currently available for use with mobile computing devices are not well suited for wireless data acquisition of time-domain data (i.e., transient signals) for mobile spectrometric applications.
the use of wireless data acquisition using smartphones and handhelds for mobile spectrometric analysis is a promising and viable alternative to the conventional approach using a wired connection.
the best wireless communications standard to use for wireless data acquisition of optical signals is Wi-Fi.

wireless data acquisition using a smartphone or a handheld is a viable option for taking part of a lab to the sample for mobile, field-portability applications.

wireless data acquisition of time-domain data using a handheld or a smart phone can be used in the field (on-site) for mobile spectrometric applications.
